definition: The Auditor General is the independent constitutional office responsible for auditing and reporting on the lawful, efficient, effective and accountable use of public resources.
mandate: Conduct financial, compliance, performance and value-for-money audits of public institutions and public funds.
authority: Issue audit reports, findings and recommendations; request evidence; and refer suspected irregularities to competent authorities.
accountability: Reports independently to the legislature and the public in accordance with the Constitution and applicable audit law.
oversightScope: National and sub-national government, public entities, grants, projects, assets and public expenditure.

definition: The Cabinet Secretary is the senior official who supports Cabinet, coordinates government policy implementation and monitors delivery across ministries and public institutions.
mandate: Coordinate Cabinet business, policy directives, cross-government priorities and implementation reporting.
authority: Convene inter-ministerial coordination, request delivery information, escalate material bottlenecks and support Cabinet decisions.
accountability: Accountable to the Head of Government for the quality of Cabinet coordination and implementation oversight.
oversightScope: Cross-government policy mandates, priority programmes, institutional delivery and executive decisions.

definition: The Minister of Finance is the political authority responsible for national fiscal policy, public finance management, the budget framework and stewardship of public funds.
mandate: Prepare and implement fiscal policy, budget proposals, revenue strategy, expenditure controls and public financial reporting.
authority: Present budget proposals, authorize delegated financial frameworks, oversee treasury operations and recommend lawful funding decisions.
accountability: Accountable to Cabinet, the legislature and the public for fiscal policy, budget execution and financial transparency.
oversightScope: Appropriations, releases, transfers, public debt, treasury, payments, financial controls and government-wide budget outcomes.

definition: The Managing Director is the executive responsible for directing an institution or state-owned enterprise, delivering its mandate and managing its people, assets, finances and services.
mandate: Translate the approved mandate and strategy into lawful operations, programmes, projects, services and measurable outcomes.
authority: Manage delegated resources, approve operational actions within authority, appoint accountable owners and enforce institutional controls.
accountability: Accountable to the board, responsible ministry or appointing authority for performance, compliance, risk and use of institutional resources.
oversightScope: Institutional strategy, operations, employees, contracts, assets, service delivery, financial performance and outcomes.
